To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AGN feedback is able to rapidly quench the star formation in galaxies and that the resulting colour change, which can be observed in large surveys, is a good indicator of the occurrence of this feedback process.

(i) the presence of feedback is indicated by the quantity tgal/tAGN, which peaks around � 0.8 Gyr for our sample of galaxies (see Fig. 2); (ii) the effect of AGN feedback is to quench star formation on a short time scale; (iii) the colour evolution of the galaxy after the feedback episode is characterized by a fast reddening in the near UV, followed by a slower reddening in the optical; (iv)
(i) AGN jets can induce a strong negative feedback, (ii) the timescale of the feedback process is of the order of a few Myr, and (iii) the feedback is detectable in the UV-optical colours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of AGN feedback in a single galaxy, which we then use as a model for a population of nearby early-type, star forming galaxies.
a new method to identify galaxies that have experienced a recent AGN feedback, based on the analysis of their colours.
the effect that the interaction between an AGN jet and the interstellar medium (ISM) has on the evolution of the star formation history in the galaxy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the framework of this study, the negative AGN feedback is a plausible mechanism to explain the presence of a large population of early-type galaxies with enhanced NUV (GALEX) g colours.
, in the context of the negative feedback model, the AGN feedback is a very powerful mechanism for quenching star formation, and is able to explain a number of observational results.
AGN feedback is a very efficient mechanism to quench star formation in massive galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the negative AGN feedback model, as described in the present paper and in the first of this series, is able to reproduce the observed colours of a sample of nearby galaxies that show signs of recent star formation.
the AGN feedback can be detected in the near-UV/optical colour of early-type galaxies, and that this colour is a good indicator of the presence, in the galaxy, of recent episodes of AGN feedback.
the presence of AGNs can be easily inferred by the enhancement of the near-UV emission in early-type galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while AGN feedback can be easily identified from the galaxy colour evolution, it is difficult to predict the exact time of its occurrence from the observed colour.

, if the jet feedback is indeed the main mechanism responsible for quenching the star formation in early-type galaxies, it can be easily identified and characterized in the near-UV/optical bands, where the signature of the feedback is a strong enhancement of the near-UV flux, with respect to an unperturbed, passive evolution.
, in the context of the negative AGN feedback model, the colour enhancement in NUV (Galex) g is an excellent tracer of the AGN feedback, which can be detected in the local Universe.
